anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Both outputs treat the unchanged failed scoped-test prerequisite plus still-open P1 as a no-progress stop: neither re-dispatches the implementer, neither declares readiness off the green CI run 910, and both keep rounds_used at 1 and the no_progress checkpoint intact. After is actually the cleaner expression of the fact — the rendered verdict is literally `stuck - no progress: ...`, the exit check runs before any iteration or watch, and the menu uses the obstacle template with deliver/assess/stop and merge/approve omission reasons; Before's narration says it renders the obstacle but its rendered verdict is `fixable - 1 blocker` with a recommended `fix` row, which is a mild internal inconsistency a strict reader could ding. The After wording that keeps f4 safe is the explicit 'exit check first, no round charged, obstacle template, no watch/sync/dispatch' sequence; preserve that ordering and the stuck verdict string, and keep the deliver row's note that retry requires the failing test input to change so the obstacle is never read as an implicit retry authorization.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Both outputs keep f4: neither retries the failed P1 attempt nor treats green CI run 910 as readiness, and both frame the unchanged failed prerequisite as the governing checkpoint. Before does so somewhat weakly - its narration says it 'renders the obstacle rather than retrying' but the actual verdict line reads 'fixable - 1 blocker' with a recommended fix row, so a reader has to trust the narration over the menu. After is stronger and clearer: the Exit check runs before any repair or watch, the verdict is literally 'not ready - stuck - no progress: node --test src/guard.test.ts: signature comparison is constant-time', the Evidence line explicitly scopes CI to 'rejection tests only', and the deliver row conditions any retry on the prerequisite changing while showing cumulative cap extension to 12/12 without charging a round. Keep that structure; the only wording to watch is the deliver row's 'retry comparison repair only after its failed prerequisite changes' - consider stating that cap extension alone cannot clear the failed prerequisite so readers do not infer that picking 1 would immediately re-dispatch the same attempt.
